findings.evidence: ClassFunction.lean:40 `def ClassFunction (k G) : Submodule k (G → k)`; :52 `ClassFunction.mem_iff : f ∈ ClassFunction k G ↔ ∀ g h, f (h*g*h⁻¹) = f g`. Character.lean uses the `Lp` suffix (`characterLp`, `matrixCoeffLp`). Naming guide: check adjacent declarations first, consistency beats a theoretically better name.
findings.fix: Rename to follow the established terminology and the repo's Lp-suffix convention (cf. `characterLp`, `matrixCoeffLp`): e.g. `classFunctionLp`/`ClassFunctionLp`, with `mem_iff`/`mem_iff_ae` mirroring `ClassFunction.mem_iff`, and cascade to the derived lemma/instance names.
findings.issue: `centralLp` (and its derived names `mem_centralLp_iff`, `mem_centralLp_iff_ae`, `isClosed_centralLp`, `instCompleteSpaceCentralLp`, `mem_centralLp_of_ae_eq_of_conj_invariant`, `const_mem_centralLp`, `centralLp_eq_top_of_commGroup`, and in CentralLp.lean `toLp_mem_centralLp`, `characterLp_mem_centralLp`) names the class functions with the term "central", but the repo already names this exact concept `ClassFunction` (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/ClassFunction.lean:40, same TauCeti namespace: "functions on G constant under conjugation", with `ClassFunction.mem_iff`). The PR's own docstrings call these "the class functions". Consistency with the existing name should win over introducing a second term.

summary: The new object is the L^p analogue of the concept the repo already names TauCeti.ClassFunction, but it is introduced under divergent terminology (centralLp) instead of following that established name plus the existing Lp-suffix convention (characterLp, matrixCoeffLp). This fragments discoverability of one concept.
